title: Auth/API 401/429 debug scratchpad - Zoe
content:
Quick scratchpad for the recurring 401/429 pattern we see for some customer API keys. Mostly notes-to-self + commands tried. Will iterate and then move into a proper runbook.

Summary of issue (observed):
- Intermittent 401s and 429s for the hosted API from a handful of API keys (customer-facing). Pattern: 401 spikes first, followed by more frequent 429s within the same hour window.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings (mostly generation traffic).
- First noticed: 2026-03-27 23:40 UTC by Alerts (rate-limit alert). Repro window: ~2026-03-28 02:00-03:30 UTC and again 2026-03-30 14:10-14:35 UTC.

Logs / examples collected:
- Curl repro showing 401 (redacted token):
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX_REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  <- {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key expired or revoked"}
  Response headers: x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d, date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 02:11:12 GMT

- Another sample showing 429 with headers:
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  {
    "error":"rate_limit_exceeded",
    "message":"Requests per minute exceeded for key"
  }
  Response headers: x-rate-limit-limit: 120, x-rate-limit-remaining: 0, x-rate-limit-reset: 2026-03-28T02:12:00Z, x-request-id: req_9f8e7d6c

- SDK call stack (Node) from customer logs (partial):
  Error: Request failed with status code 401
    at createHttpError (.../node_modules/axios/index.js:...)
    at instance.request (...)
    at Object.generate (redwood-sdk/lib/client.js:123:45)

Hypothesis list (ranked):
1) Key rotation / expiry pipeline: keys are expiring unexpectedly due to an automated rotation job that revokes old keys before the client fetches new one. Evidence: 401s often precede 429s and are short-lived.
2) Client-side caching of credentials: clients using long-lived token cached in warm instances -> when key is rotated they keep using old token causing 401 spikes.
3) Per-key quota is small and we do aggressive retries: client retries (exponential backoff not implemented) cause burst that flips 401 to 429 when a new key is created and historical requests replay.
4) Mis-routed traffic to a regional rate limiter (edge case): requests get routed to a different region where quota has already been consumed.
5) SDK auth bug: older SDK versions signed requests incorrectly (we saw a customer using v0.9.1 vs recommended 1.x).

Commands / checks I ran (timestamps UTC):
- 2026-03-28 02:14: curl -v to reproduce (see above)
- 2026-03-28 02:20: pulled internal audit logs for key sk_live_XXXX_REDACTED: found automated rotation event at 2026-03-28 02:11:05 (metadata: rotated_by=key-rotation-service, reason=schedule)
- 2026-03-28 02:25: queried quota service:
  GET /internal/quotas?key_id=key_abc123 -> {"limit_minute":120, "used_minute":118}
- 2026-03-28 02:27: inspected CDN/edge traces for req_0a1b2c3d -> routed through edge-eu-1 (odd: customer is NA)
- 2026-03-30 14:18: asked customer for SDK version; they replied v0.9.1 and said they rely on env var rotation that updates process env every 10m (no graceful restart)

Immediate notes from above:
- The rotation event at 02:11:05 matches the 401 at 02:11:12 (7s later) -> likely race where key revoked while client still sending previous key.
- x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 indicates the key hit a per-minute limit after a burst (maybe client retried quickly after expiry).
- Edge routing mismatch suggests our smart routing may be sending some traffic to non-optimal region; if quota counts are region-scoped this could explain per-region exhaustion.

Reproduction plan (manual):
1) Simulate rotation race locally:
   - Start a small script that uses the old key and continues to send requests while rotation job runs.
   - Confirm 401s during transitional window.
2) Simulate retry storm:
   - Make a test client that retries immediately on 401 (no backoff) and observe whether the same API key hits 429 soon after.
3) Test with latest SDK vs v0.9.1 to check signing/auth differences.

Next immediate actions (TODOs):
- [ ] Add more detailed logging to the key-rotation service (timestamp of revoke, affected key ids, region tags). (owner: infra/key-rotation)
- [ ] Add a short grace window (30s) where rotated keys remain accepted to avoid immediate 401s during rollout. Quick mitigation if approved. (owner: infra)
- [ ] Contact customer and ask them to upgrade SDK to 1.x and implement exponential backoff for 401->retry path. (owner: CS)
- [ ] Create an alert rule that correlates 401 spikes followed by 429 within 10 minutes for the same key (owner: SRE)
- [ ] For suspected region routing issue: run a trace for next incident and route to local quota service for validation. (owner: networking)
- [ ] Open a support ticket with request IDs: req_0a1b2c3d and req_9f8e7d6c and include audit logs.

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts:
- Grace window may mask real compromised key problems — need to limit to rotating keys only (tagged) and have strict audit trail.
- Could we also return a more specific header on 401 that indicates "revoked" vs "expired"? That helps customers decide whether to retry or re-fetch token.
- Investigate whether our SDKs should automatically pick up env VAR changes (signal-based reload) instead of relying on process restart.

Attachments to add later:
- raw log snippets (redacted), timelines, screenshots of quota dashboard, customer's SDK version and sample code.

If I forget: escalate to infra on-call and include this doc link + request IDs.

End of scratchpad.
